title: What I Talk About When I Talk About Running
author: Haruki Murakami

title: The Whole Story
author: John Mackey
oneLiner: John Mackey’s memoir follows him from a drifting Austin dropout to cofounder and longtime CEO of Whole Foods Market, then through expansion, conflict, public pressure, and a late-life search for meaning beyond the company.

title: The Presentation Secrets of Steve Jobs
author: Carmine Gallo
oneLiner: Carmine Gallo’s book follows Steve Jobs as a model for public speaking and product launches, not as a full biography.

title: Sam Walton: The Inside Story of America's Richest Man
author: Vance H. Trimble

title: Richer, Wiser, Happier
author: William Green
oneLiner: William Green’s Richer, Wiser, Happier follows a journalist-turned-investor-reader as he interviews major money managers and tries to understand not just how they got rich, but how they built lives that could survive risk, failure, and change.

title: Money Talks, Bullsh*t Walks
author: Ben Johnson
oneLiner: Ben Johnson’s Money Talks, Bullsh*t Walks follows Sam Zell, the blunt Chicago real-estate investor who built fortunes buying distressed assets, then took on Tribune Company and helped drive it into bankruptcy.

title: Invention: A Life
author: James Dyson
oneLiner: James Dyson’s memoir follows the life of an inventor turned manufacturer: a boy from north Norfolk who loved art and running, lost his father young, met and married Deirdre, trained at the Royal College of Art, and then spent decades turning practical frustrations into products, companies, schools, and eventually an electric car and a farming empire.

title: Open
author: Andre Agassi
oneLiner: Andre Agassi’s memoir follows Andre Agassi, the former tennis prodigy turned champion, from a childhood shaped by a domineering father and punishing training into the highs, injuries, public rebellions, relationships, and self-reconstruction that defined his pro career.

title: Shoe Dog
author: Phil Knight
oneLiner: Shoe Dog is Phil Knight’s memoir of becoming the founder of Nike, beginning with a young Oregon runner’s decision to turn a vague, risky dream into a business and following that choice through years of improvisation, loyalty, panic, and growth.
